headline: TUDOR GOLD DRILLS 9.00 G/T AU OVER 9.5M AT TREATY CREEK — 43.29 g/t spike; Golden Triangle step-out confirms depth extension
snippet: Tudor Gold's Treaty Creek joint venture in BC's Golden Triangle reported a drill hole returning 9.00 g/t gold over 9.50 metres, including a high-grade interval of 43.29 g/t gold over 1.20 metres drilled down-dip from previous high-grade surface samples — extending the known mineralised footprint at depth and reinforcing Treaty Creek's status as one of the most significant undeveloped gold systems in northwest British Columbia. The property already hosts the Goldstorm porphyry-gold system alongside multiple high-grade structural zones; continued positive step-out results at depth add district-scale resource potential ahead of an anticipated resource update.

headline: STORM EXPLORATION CONFIRMS VMS SOURCE IN ALL 8 HOLES AT GOLD STANDARD ONT — Sulphide up to 70%; 7km conductor; assays due Q1/2027
snippet: Storm Exploration (TSX-V: STRM) confirmed a volcanogenic massive sulphide system in all eight holes of its latest program at the Gold Standard project in northwestern Ontario, with the best 5.52-metre interval from 144 to 149.52 metres containing up to 70% sulphide — pyrrhotite, pyrite, sphalerite and chalcopyrite — interpreted as the source of a 7-kilometre geophysical conductor originally defined by Inco in 1969. Assays are expected in early Q1 2027 with drilling resuming in Q2; a positive result confirming copper-zinc grades consistent with the mineralogy could significantly re-rate this early-stage VMS explorer on the TSX-V.

headline: CRITICAL METALS LOCKS IN 100% TANBREEZ OFFTAKE AND $264.5M WAR CHEST — Greenland rare earth giant sets 2027 construction roadmap
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (Nasdaq: CRML) announced November 11 that it has met all 2026 objectives — including securing 100% offtake coverage for the Tanbreez rare earth project in Greenland, completing ownership to 92.5% after government approvals, and holding $264.5 million in cash with 194.2 million shares outstanding. With offtake fully locked across its Saudi and Western partners and Greenland government support firmly established, the 2027 roadmap moves Tanbreez — one of the world's largest rare earth deposits at an estimated $3 billion NPV — toward a construction decision on the $800M–$1B capex project.

headline: GALANTAS GOLD DRILLS NEW SKARN DISCOVERY AT INDIANA CHILE — 18m at 1.18 g/t Au; first bulk-width gold not confined to narrow structures
snippet: Galantas Gold reported an 18-metre intersection at 1.18 g/t gold from 269 to 287 metres depth, including 4 metres at 2.36 g/t gold, in a newly discovered skarn at its Indiana project in Chile — the first documented gold mineralisation at Indiana not restricted to narrow vein structures. The skarn environment suggests the potential for bulk-tonnage mineralisation at depth, distinguishing this from the narrow-vein systems that characterise most Chilean gold exploration projects and opening a larger resource model than the company has previously modelled.

headline: AUSTRALIAN GOLD & COPPER HITS POLYMETALLIC ZONE AT EVERGREEN NSW — 16m at 2.3g/t Au, 70g/t Ag, 12.2% Pb+Zn from 112m
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper (ASX: AGC) reported RC hole EGRC018 at its Evergreen project in Hillston, New South Wales intersecting 16 metres at 2.3 g/t gold, 70 g/t silver, 1.4% copper and 12.2% combined lead-zinc from 112 metres — a polymetallic result that expands Evergreen's economic profile across four simultaneous commodity streams. The combination of precious and base metals in a single broad shallow zone is unusual for the Hillston region and raises the prospect of a multi-commodity resource with favourable processing economics.

headline: ATALAYA SNAPS UP THARSIS MINING FOR €125M — Zero equity dilution builds 50km Iberian copper district
snippet: Atalaya Mining (LSE/TSX: ATYM) disclosed a €125 million acquisition of Tharsis Mining alongside its Q3 2026 results, structured as €75 million upfront and €50 million deferred with no equity dilution for existing shareholders — a deal that extends Atalaya's footprint in Spain's Iberian Pyrite Belt to roughly 50 kilometres. The Tharsis sulphide deposits are geologically compatible with Atalaya's existing Riotinto processing infrastructure, potentially enabling ore blending that could increase throughput and extend mine life at its record-profit copper operation.

headline: COPPER: WHY RISING SUPPLY WON'T PREVENT A 2027 SQUEEZE — FXStreet: AI data centres, mine delays set up 150k-600kt deficit
snippet: An FXStreet copper outlook published November 12 argues that despite new mine capacity from Kamoa-Kakula and other projects, the combination of AI data centre copper demand, EV production ramp and ongoing disruptions at Grasberg create a likely supply squeeze in 2027 even as short-term LME prices face macro pressure from US rate hike expectations. Bank deficit forecasts for 2026 alone range from 150,000 tonnes (ICSG) to 600,000 tonnes (ING), with Red Cloud's contrarian surplus forecast of 126,000 tonnes the main dissenting view — a spread that reflects deep uncertainty about China's downstream demand recovery timeline.

headline: RECORD 1,231 TONNE GOLD DEMAND IN Q3 CANNOT STOP $3,866 SELLOFF — Rate hike pricing overwhelms all-time-high fundamentals
snippet: Central bank and institutional gold buying hit a record 1,231 tonnes in Q3 2026 — the highest single-quarter total on record — yet the gold price has sold off to $3,866 as Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations triggered by October's hot CPI data dominate short-term market positioning. Crux Investor argues the fundamental backdrop of record demand and structural supply constraints has not changed, and that the correction is a futures-market positioning event rather than a reversal of the underlying bull market thesis.

headline: AFTER THE RUSH FOR REFUGE, A REALITY CHECK ON THE GOLD-SILVER ROUT — What $3,866 gold and $50 silver actually mean for junior mining investors
snippet: Crux Investor's post-market analysis of the November 12 selloff examines the asymmetric impact on different segments of the junior mining market — identifying royalty and streaming companies as showing relative institutional strength, while drill-stage and development-stage juniors face disproportionate retail risk-off selling. The piece argues that for investors with a 12-to-24-month time horizon, the gap between current junior miner share prices and the fundamentals of their underlying assets is as wide as it was at the 2022 lows.

headline: 5 GOLD MINERS THAT GIVE A DIFFERENT WAY TO PLAY $4,000 GOLD — Wheaton, Kinross, Barrick, Agnico among Motley Fool's November picks
snippet: The Motley Fool's November 11 analysis identifies Wheaton Precious Metals, Kinross, Barrick and Agnico Eagle among five gold miners offering diverse paths to gold exposure beyond owning bullion directly — favouring companies with low cash costs, royalty or streaming structures, or significant operational leverage to a price recovery. The piece notes that gold miners have dramatically underperformed the gold price in 2026 despite record earnings and free cash flow, creating a valuation gap the author expects to close once December Fed rate hike certainty is fully priced in.
